First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(5{n}^{2}-4)(5{n}^{2}+4)}{{n}^{2}(3-40{n}^{2})}=\frac{25{n}^{4}-16}{3{n}^{2}-40{n}^{4}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{25{n}^{4}-16}{3{n}^{2}-40{n}^{4}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-40{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{25{n}^{4}-16}{3{n}^{2}-40{n}^{4}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{25{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{16}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{3{n}^{2}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{40{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(25-\frac{16}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{3}{{n}^{2}}-40)} \\  & =\frac{25-0}{0-40} \\  & =-\frac{5}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $-\frac{5}{8}.$
